sections.title: Classification of Functions (One-One & Onto)
sections.content: One-One (Injective): Every x has a unique y. Check by strictly increasing/decreasing derivative (f'(x) > 0 or f'(x) < 0). Onto (Surjective): Range equals Codomain. If a function is both, it is Bijective (invertible).

sections.title: Indeterminate Forms & 1^∞ Limits
sections.content: For limits of the form 1^∞, use the formula: lim (x->a) f(x)^g(x) = e^L, where L = lim (x->a) [f(x) - 1] * g(x). This bypasses complex logarithmic expansions.

sections.title: Differentiability (LHD & RHD)
sections.content: A function is differentiable at x = a if Left Hand Derivative (LHD) = Right Hand Derivative (RHD). Graphically, it means a unique tangent can be drawn (no sharp corners/kinks). Differentiability strictly implies continuity, but not vice versa.

sections.title: Implicit and Parametric Differentiation
sections.content: Implicit: Differentiate both sides w.r.t x, treating y as a function of x (append dy/dx). Parametric: If x=f(t) and y=g(t), then dy/dx = (dy/dt) / (dx/dt). For second derivative, d²y/dx² = d/dx(dy/dx) * (dt/dx).

sections.title: Application of Derivatives: Tangents & Normals
sections.content: The slope of the tangent at (x1, y1) is m = (dy/dx) at that point. Tangent equation: y - y1 = m(x - x1). The normal is perpendicular, so its slope is -1/m. Normal equation: y - y1 = (-1/m)(x - x1).

sections.title: Monotonicity (Increasing & Decreasing)
sections.content: If f'(x) > 0 on an interval, f(x) is strictly increasing. If f'(x) < 0, it is strictly decreasing. Critical points occur where f'(x) = 0 or is undefined; these are candidates for local maxima/minima.

sections.title: Common Mistakes
sections.content:
1) Incorrectly calculating the second derivative in parametric form by just dividing d²y/dt² by d²x/dt².
2) Assuming f'(x) = 0 guarantees a maximum or minimum (it could be a point of inflection).
3) Applying L'Hopital's rule when the limit is NOT in 0/0 or ∞/∞ form.

sections.title: Quick Summary
sections.content: Level 2 introduces deeper analysis: checking invertibility (bijections), solving 1^∞ limits, analyzing sharp corners (differentiability), and applying derivatives to graphs (tangents, increasing/decreasing).

tricks.title: The 1^∞ Limit Shortcut
tricks.explanation: Directly apply e^[lim(g(x) * (f(x)-1))] for limits of form 1^∞.

tricks.title: Derivative of Inverse Function
tricks.explanation: If g(x) is the inverse of f(x), then g'(x) = 1 / f'(g(x)). This allows finding the derivative of an inverse without actually calculating the inverse function.

tricks.title: Length of Subtangent and Subnormal
tricks.explanation: Length of tangent = |y√(1+1/m²)|. Length of normal = |y√(1+m²)|. Length of Subtangent = |y/m|. Length of Subnormal = |ym| (where m = dy/dx).
tricks.example: Instantly solves coordinate geometry AOD questions without line equations.

tricks.title: Number of Onto Functions
tricks.explanation: From set A (m elements) to set B (n elements) where m ≥ n: n^m - nC1(n-1)^m + nC2(n-2)^m - ...

tricks.title: Implicit Differentiation Shortcut
tricks.explanation: For an implicit function f(x,y) = 0, dy/dx = - [∂f/∂x] / [∂f/∂y]. (Partially differentiate w.r.t x keeping y constant, divided by vice versa).
